properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 28 at 8:28AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Previous rainfall working through the basin has caused river levels
on the St. Johns at Sanford to continue to slowly rise and is
forecast to go above record Flood Stage of 9.0, which it currently
sits. While remaining within Major Flood Stage, the river is forecast
to remain steady between 9.0 to 9.2 feet through at least early next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river currently sits at Record Flood Stage and is forecast to
exceed this number slightly.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Flooding becomes more significant to the
Sanford waterfront area. Water approaches low lying areas on the
waterfront.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 9.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.2 feet
this weekend. The river is then expected to remain steady within
Major Flood Stage between 9.0 to 9.2 feet through at least early
next week.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 900 PM EST.

properties.description:

forecast.

Beware of the dangers of crossing flooded roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

properties.description:

Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 28 at 8:13AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Past heavy rainfall working its way through the basin will cause
levels on the St Johns River at Astor to remain steady within Major
Flood Stage between 4.3 and 4.4 feet well into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 4.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 4.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to remain generally steady
between 4.3 and 4.4 feet well into next week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 28 at 8:17AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall across the upper St. Johns River has caused levels
near Cocoa to remain within Major Flood Stage, well above its
previous record flood stage. The river level trends are forecast to
follow a very slow decline through Major Flood Stage through next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The crest has exceeded the previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 AM EST Saturday the stage was 18.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 AM EST Saturday was 18.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to show a very slow decline from
18.2 feet to 17.7 feet from this weekend and through next week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

least mid next week.
